claim: The same decay at a step it suits, k = 0.5 per hour at Δt = 0.1 hour, passes the accuracy check: halving the step moves x by under 2e-5 molecules, 2% of what the check allows. So the refusal of the stiff decay is the check working, not a check that refuses everything.
derivation: dx/dt = −k·x with k = 0.5 per hour, x₀ = 1000 molecules, Δt = 0.1 hour, tolerance 1e-6, over N = 20 coarse steps.
By E3 the coarse run after n steps is x₀·R(−0.05)^n and the fine run after 2n half steps is x₀·R(−0.025)^(2n).

Computed with exact fractions, the largest |R(−0.05)^n − R(−0.025)^(2n)| over n = 1 … 20 is 1.8753e-8, at n = 20: a deviation of 1.8753e-5 molecules. (Each run is within n·|z|⁵/120 of e^(−0.05n), 2.6e-9·n and 1.6e-10·n, so the deviation is about their difference.)

The scale is the coarse run's largest |x|, x₀ = 1000 at the start, so the allowance is 1e-6 × 1000 = 1e-3 molecules, and the worst deviation uses 1.9% of it. Rounding, under 1e-10, cannot change the verdict.

anchors.need: None: a hand-built oracle model, taken from no paper.
